source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 11–12. All 51 exact original records are hashed, including the written/read annotation at 12:3 and the source form annotation at 12:9. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Preserve Miriam first, both accusers and the repeated Cushite-marriage statement; do not identify the unnamed woman as Zipporah or invent a second marriage chronology.
Keep the plural challenge and claimed prophetic participation of both Miriam and Aaron, followed by the terse divine hearing.
Follow the humble adjective in the written/read record, preserving the strong comparison and all-human scope; note meek/afflicted semantic possibilities without asserting authorship.

Read the compressed your prophet construction as a prophet among you and the divine name as subject apposition; inclusive generic reference fits the audience, while vision/dream parallelism remains poetry.
Retain the explicit contrast, servant title and house image; trusted conveys the reliable/entrusted range with faithful as an alternative in a note.
Keep mouth-to-mouth rather than replace with face-to-face, retain form of the LORD without harmonizing other vision passages, and preserve the concluding accusatory question.
Keep the sudden double discovery and snow image, with tsaraat terminology consistent with Leviticus rather than a confident modern diagnosis; do not transfer her condition to Aaron.
Keep the plea, deferential title and first-person plural confession shared by Aaron and Miriam; no absolution is supplied.
Preserve the distressing death-at-birth, womb and half-consumed flesh comparison without euphemism or adding a specific diagnosis.
Keep the short cry and both pleading particles; do not replace them with now or add a longer prayer.
Preserve the hypothetical paternal humiliation, face image, both seven-day periods and forced exclusion followed by readmission; do not endorse the analogy as present-day advice.
Retain Miriam’s exclusion, duration and the whole people waiting for her return; no claim of an explicitly narrated cure is added.
